flow_name: Admin Dashboard Navigation and Management Flow
preserved_behavior: Order list display and file upload image preview state tracking are maintained.
changed_behavior: A fully modernized, dark-themed responsive dashboard interface using Vanilla CSS variables and premium glassmorphic visual widgets. Seamless reactive state transitions, real-time KPI status indicators, and clean form inputs replace the current barebones structure.
user_goal: Allow Shop Managers and Administrators to monitor e-commerce performance metrics, process orders (with refund control), and create/manage products with rich image previews.

screens.name: KPI Dashboard Overview
screens.purpose: High-level summary of total sales, total orders, refunds, and low stock warnings to help managers assess shop status.

screens.name: Orders Management
screens.purpose: Detailed table of orders with filter by status, search, and action triggers for refunds or viewing details.

screens.name: Products Management & Add Product Form
screens.purpose: Manage catalog, view existing products, and add new products with R2 drag-and-drop file upload and safe image previews.

transitions.trigger: Click Orders in sidebar or Click Sales/Orders KPI card details

accessibility_notes: Provide visual focus outlines for keyboard navigation across all interactive widgets.
Order status badges must use high-contrast text color combinations (e.g. green on dark-green bg) to satisfy WCAG AA standards.
Image preview components must declare explicit screen reader alt text during loading and post-upload phases.

analytics_events.trigger: Click refund button on order row

api_needs.purpose: Fetch KPI aggregate metrics (total sales, active orders, refund rates, inventory stats)
api_needs.notes: Used to populate the dashboard overview cards.

api_needs.purpose: Fetch and page orders with filter by status
api_needs.notes: Required for dynamic populating of the Orders table.

api_needs.purpose: Submit new product details and trigger R2 upload
api_needs.notes: Handles product creation and asset storage in Cloudflare R2.

open_questions: Should we support CSV export of orders and products for store managers?
Do we want charts (e.g., lightweight canvas/SVG line graphs) for total sales over time, or are aggregate numeric metrics sufficient for the MVP?
